opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted; write is the maximum for this employee. Requested write is within policy, recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Casey Wu (E005) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on Casey Wu's employment status: one (HR) says full-time Payroll Specialist, allowing write for Source Code; the other (Security) says contractor with basic security training, capping access at read. Given the conflicting facts, I apply the more restrictive, policy-compliant outcome. Under the contractor interpretation, write is not permitted (basic training, not advanced), so the maximum is read. Granting read is the safe decision that does not exceed policy under either interpretation.
